comments.why: Rob Pike explains the difference between concurrency and parallelism.
comments.text: yeah, basically. a lot of people do not know, but async/await does have NOTHING do to with threads or processes. you can use threads with async/await, but you do not. async/await basically means you are running your "green threads"/tasks/promises on a event loop, the event loop can be either single threaded or it can run the stuff on multiple threads. a lot of people just did not get the difference between concurrency vs. parallelism. threads and processes are basically parallelism, while concurrency is async programming. good talk about that stuff from rob pike (go): [VIDEO]

comments.author: duped
comments.why: Cited for distinction between concurrency and parallelism.
comments.text: As with all benchmarks, benchmark your workload. The tech empower stuff is gamed, like all rankings. But first and foremost, concurrency is not parallelism [1]. In my practical experience dealing with both, asycn is a language semantic for concurrency, threads are an OS feature for parallelism. It's a little nonsensical to ask the pros/cons since they are different entirely ; you can use both at the same time (and in practice most async implementations use threads) [1] [VIDEO] "Concurrency is not Parallelism" talk by Rob Pike.
